planSpec.stakes: whether fear of judgment blocks work
planSpec.requiredBeat: Use mortality to turn fear into chosen action

examples.scenario: Selene, a sculptor, locks a Brooklyn studio at 10:00 at night after hiding the same unfinished figure under cloth for weeks. A friend's sudden funeral and Josh's lake story have made her avoidance feel childish and human at once. The gallery deadline is nine days away.
examples.whatToDo: Selene should uncover the figure and finish the next rough surface tomorrow morning. Judgment is real, but the clock is real too.
examples.whyItMatters: Mortality does not erase fear. It makes fear answer to the finite chance to make and share the work.

questions.prompt: Maeve hears about a lake death and keeps ignoring people who love her. What does mortality as a value filter ask?
choices: Maeve should wait until grief becomes clearer before reaching out.
Maeve should turn the memorial into proof that life is too fragile for effort.
Maeve should return one call because avoidance now has a visible cost.
questions.explanation: Josh's death makes avoidance concrete. Mortality does not remove grief, but it can lower the authority of fear and hiding.

questions.prompt: Cassian studies Becker and wonders whether ambition is noble or fear-driven. Which distinction helps most?
choices: Does the project serve living values, or mainly protect a symbolic self from death terror?
Will the project be remembered long enough to justify the ambition?
Can the project make Cassian feel less ordinary than his classmates?
questions.explanation: Becker does not make all legacy projects empty. The key test is whether the project serves life or ego defense.

questions.prompt: Devika's donor wants larger atrium lettering while resisting patient-care funding. What is the best diagnosis?
choices: The donor's recognition requirement is harmless because the hospital still gets money.
The immortality project is starting to outrank the care it claims to serve.
The hospital should reject named gifts because legacy motives corrupt giving.
questions.explanation: Immortality projects can serve life or distort it. Here the symbolic self is competing with patient impact.

questions.prompt: Malcolm reads his mentor's obituary and questions another year of prestige work. Which response keeps the filter practical?
choices: Malcolm should quit immediately because death makes planning look timid.
Malcolm should schedule the serious career conversation he keeps avoiding.
Malcolm should stay put because prestige is one way to survive symbolically.
questions.explanation: Mortality clarifies values; it does not demand reckless theater. Malcolm needs a truthful next conversation.

questions.prompt: Oriel keeps apology drafts unsent because pride protects the flawless self. What does death awareness change?
choices: It proves Oriel should apologize only if the family reunion goes badly.
It makes the old argument easier to win with urgency.
It shrinks pride by showing that repair matters while the relationship is alive.
questions.explanation: Mortality reduces the value of ego protection. Oriel's apology creates present meaning that pride has been blocking.

questions.prompt: Selene fears judgment on an unfinished sculpture, but funerals have made time feel finite. Which action fits best?
choices: Uncover the sculpture and finish the next rough surface despite fear.
Hide the work until fear disappears, so the final piece is cleaner.
Switch to a safer project that will attract less judgment.
questions.explanation: Mortality does not erase judgment. It asks whether fear deserves more authority than the remaining chance to make the work.

questions.prompt: A friend says everyone dies, so nothing matters. Which reply carries the sharper turn?
choices: Finite time makes choosing well more urgent, not less meaningful.
Death matters only when someone close dies suddenly.
Effort matters when it can create a remembered public legacy.
questions.explanation: The hard edge rejects fatalism. Death filters values so care can be spent with more courage and less vanity.

questions.prompt: When a leader protects reputation at the expense of employees, which Becker lens is most useful?
choices: The leader is choosing a practical way to keep authority stable.
The leader may be defending a symbolic self as if it were more important than living people.
The leader should build a larger legacy so employees understand the sacrifice.
questions.explanation: Becker's lens shows how symbolic survival can become dangerous. Reputation cannot outrank the people harmed by its defense.

questions.prompt: A reader wants to use mortality without becoming morbid. Which practice best fits?
choices: Read obituaries until ordinary fears feel embarrassing enough to ignore.
Make a legacy plan centered on being remembered by as many people as possible.
Name one fear that shrinks the day, then choose an action that serves a value despite it.
questions.explanation: The practice uses death awareness to reduce fear's authority. It points toward present values rather than morbid rumination or fame.

reviewCards.front: What is mortality as a value filter?
reviewCards.back: It is using death awareness to see which concerns are ego protection and which values deserve care while time is finite.

reviewCards.front: What does Josh's death make visible?
reviewCards.back: It makes avoidance costly. Fear, shame, and embarrassment lose some authority when the ending becomes real.

reviewCards.front: What does Ernest Becker add?
reviewCards.back: Becker explains how humans manage death terror by building symbolic selves through achievement, family, culture, ideology, and legacy.

reviewCards.front: When do immortality projects become dangerous?
reviewCards.back: They become dangerous when protecting a symbolic self matters more than truth, present meaning, or living people.

reviewCards.front: Why is the final lesson not fatalism?
reviewCards.back: Because finite time raises the stakes of choosing well. Death is used to clarify care, not erase it.

implementationPlan.title: Filter Fear Through Mortality
implementationPlan.coreSkill: Use death awareness to lower the authority of vanity and fear. Do not brood for drama. Let finitude point you toward one action that creates present meaning.

ifThenPlans.context: A small fear runs the day
ifThenPlans.plan: If embarrassment or rejection controls you, then ask how much of your finite life that fear deserves.
If being remembered becomes the goal, then ask who is served by the work while they are alive.
If apology feels humiliating, then compare that feeling with the cost of losing the relationship unrepaired.
If mortality turns into rumination, then choose one concrete act of love, craft, service, or courage.

implementationPlan.twentyFourHourChallenge: Write one fear that shrank today. Take one action that serves a chosen value while that fear is still present.
implementationPlan.weeklyPractice: Once a week, review your biggest worry through mortality: will this matter at the end, and what living value deserves the next hour?

memorableLines.text: Death is no longer an idea on a poster.
memorableLines.why: It makes mortality concrete rather than abstract.

memorableLines.text: Mortality clarifies because it removes the fantasy of unlimited postponement.
memorableLines.why: It states why death awareness changes action.

memorableLines.text: Death makes false importance feel thin.
memorableLines.why: It captures the chapter's value filter in one line.
